question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: Result = SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the UTF-8 encoding of P, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

Lines. The text is split at every line feed (000A) only; the empty piece after a final line feed is a line like any other. From each line ONE trailing carriage return (000D) is removed, if present; any other carriage return stays in the line as an ordinary character. Lines are read in order; a line made only of WS characters (or empty) is skipped.
INDENT = the longest prefix of the line made of space (0020) and tab (0009) only; CONTENT = the rest. CONTENT is never empty here (R2).
Full-line comment: CONTENT begins with NUMBER SIGN (0023) -> the line is dropped; CURRENT is unchanged.

Trailing comment. In CONTENT, the marker is the NUMBER SIGN at the smallest position k (k >= 1) such that the character at k-1 is WS, the character at k+1 is WS or k is the last position, and CONTENT contains no LT character at any position other than k-1. With a marker, CODE = CONTENT before position k-1 with its trailing WS run removed; without one, CODE = CONTENT unchanged (trailing WS kept). So a NUMBER SIGN glued to text on either side is content, and a line holding an LT anywhere but just before the sign has no trailing comment at all CITED FIDELITY package.

Column-0 line (INDENT empty). Split CODE into NAME = its longest prefix of non-WS characters and TAIL = what follows NAME with its whole leading WS run removed. The split FAILS when NAME is empty (CODE is empty or begins with WS — a no-break space, a byte-order mark, a vertical tab) or when TAIL contains an LT character. On success: if NAME is an uppercase letter A-Z, then zero or more of A-Z 0-9 "-", then a final ":", the colon is dropped. If NAME is now an uppercase letter A-Z followed by zero or more of A-Z 0-9 "-", the line starts a NEW directive: NAME, and ARGS and ATTRS from R8 applied to TAIL, no continuations; it becomes CURRENT. Known and unknown names alike.

Any other column-0 line (split failed, or NAME not of that form): if CURRENT exists, CODE is appended VERBATIM to its continuations — no attribute extraction, no trimming; otherwise the line is dropped. A leading byte-order mark therefore drops the first directive line of a file.

Attribute extraction over a piece S yields (BODY, A). Repeat: find the EARLIEST keyword occurrence K in S — K one of CITED, EARNED, ANCHOR, immediately preceded by a run of one or more WS characters — whose remainder R (everything after K) begins with WS and can be cut into a non-empty all-WS head and a non-empty tail containing no LT. If none exists, stop. Otherwise value = R with leading and trailing WS removed (possibly empty); if A already holds a NON-EMPTY value for K, A[K] = old value, one space, value; otherwise A[K] = value; then S = S cut just before the WS run preceding K. BODY = the final S with leading and trailing WS removed. Consequences the oracle pins: the first qualifying keyword swallows the rest of the line, later keywords included ("x CITED a EARNED b" -> CITED = "a EARNED b"); a keyword that begins S, or lacks WS after it, or has only a single WS after it and nothing more, stays in BODY; more than one extraction per piece happens only when an LT blocks an earlier keyword's remainder CITED FIDELITY package.

Indented line (INDENT not empty): if no CURRENT, the line is dropped. Otherwise apply R8 to CODE: BODY is appended to CURRENT's continuations (even when empty), and each (K, value) of A, in A's order, is stored into CURRENT's ATTRS REPLACING any earlier value for K — an earlier CITED is overwritten, never joined CITED FIDELITY package.

ATTRS order = the order in which each keyword was FIRST stored into that directive (a replaced key keeps its place); within one R8 run, keywords are stored in extraction order (rightmost occurrence first).

P. For each directive in reading order: one line = NAME, then (only if ARGS is non-empty) one space and ARGS, then for each ATTRS entry in order one space, the keyword, one space, the value (an empty value leaves a trailing space); then one line per continuation = two spaces and the continuation text. P = all lines, each followed by one line feed. No directive at all -> P is a single line feed.
